chat.why: Same skill as the live mmlu_pro set (school/university knowledge multiple choice, letter answer), but 4 options instead of 10 and the questions are original 2020 MMLU items.

math_code.why: Only the 5 math/statistics subjects of 57 are math, and they are 4-option multiple choice, not boxed or closed-form answers.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, one text question with a short answer

3.model: Claude Opus 4.5 / Gemini 3 Pro (mean of 0.956 and 0.959)

mmlu_redux.results_where: HELM MMLU per-instance predictions (79 models, all 57 MMLU subjects): https://storage.googleapis.com/crfm-helm-public/mmlu/benchmark_output/releases/v1.13.0/runs_to_run_suites.json ; TAUR-Lab CoT outputs (14 models, full MMLU 14,042): https://huggingface.co/collections/TAUR-Lab/cot-analysis-project-66bbb9e5e0156e65059895f5 (join to MMLU-Redux by question text and re-grade with the corrected labels)
mmlu_redux.overlap: MMLU-Redux questions are original MMLU test questions; the live mmlu_pro set reuses 6,810 filtered original-MMLU questions (options expanded to 10), so some stems can appear in both: remove them by question-text match.
mmlu_redux.summary: 5,700 MMLU questions (100 from each of 57 subjects) re-checked by experts, with an error label per question (ok, wrong ground truth, no/multiple correct answers, unclear). Cleaned 4-option knowledge multiple choice: a close, larger stand-in for mmlu_pro, and per-model results exist through HELM MMLU on the same questions.

chat.why: Open-ended two-turn instructions (writing, roleplay, extraction, STEM, humanities, reasoning, math, coding) scored 1-10 by a GPT-4 judge or by pairwise preference; only 39 of 80 have a reference answer.

math_code.why: Only 20 of 80 questions are math or coding, two-turn, and graded by a 1-10 judge rather than a checked answer or tests.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, open-ended chat

mt_bench.results_where: https://huggingface.co/spaces/lmsys/mt-bench (data/mt_bench/model_answer: 34 models' answers; model_judgment/gpt-4_single.jsonl and gpt-4_pair.jsonl); human pairwise votes for 6 models: https://huggingface.co/datasets/lmsys/mt_bench_human_judgments
mt_bench.summary: 80 two-turn open-ended prompts in 8 categories (10 each), judged 1-10 by GPT-4; the HF dataset holds 3.3k expert pairwise votes and 2.4k GPT-4 pairwise votes over 6 models. Too small, old and judge-graded to stand in for Yugos questions, but the public per-question grades for 34 older models (and RouterBench's copy) are usable router training signal; scores are on a 1-10 scale, so no level anchors.

chat.why: Same skill and grader as the live hotpotqa set (multi-hop question over Wikipedia paragraphs, short answer scored by answer F1 plus supporting-paragraph F1), with 2-4 hops and 20 paragraphs (~2,500 tokens).

math_code.why: different skill: reading Wikipedia paragraphs for a short factual answer

agentic.why: different skill: no tools (paragraphs are given in the prompt)

1.model: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct (zero-shot direct; 4,834 MuSiQue dev rows that appear to include the unanswerable twins; metric not stated)

2.model: GPT-4o / Claude 3.5 Sonnet (mean of 0.701 and 0.704, same setting)

musique.results_where: https://huggingface.co/collections/TAUR-Lab/cot-analysis-project-66bbb9e5e0156e65059895f5 (config musique_all, 4,834 rows, is_correct per question for 14 models incl. GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Llama 3.1 8B/70B, Gemini 1.5)
musique.summary: Multi-hop questions (2-4 hops) built by chaining single-hop questions, each with 20 Wikipedia paragraphs (supporting + distractors); the HF copy has 19,938 train + 2,417 dev answerable questions, test answers are hidden behind a leaderboard. The closest public match to Yugos's hotpotqa part, harder to shortcut, and 14 models' per-question outcomes are public.

chat.why: Long story-based soft-reasoning puzzles (murder mystery, object placement, team allocation; ~800-1,400 tokens) with a short multiple-choice answer, the same flavour as the live bbeh set.

math_code.why: different skill: narrative reasoning with a choice answer, no math or code

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, one text question with a short answer

1.model: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct (zero-shot CoT, question-weighted mean of 70.4/55.5/44.0)

2.model: GPT-4o / Claude 3.5 Sonnet (zero-shot CoT, weighted means 0.730 and 0.783)

musr.results_where: https://huggingface.co/collections/TAUR-Lab/cot-analysis-project-66bbb9e5e0156e65059895f5 (configs mm_musr/op_musr/ta_musr, 14 models incl. GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Llama 3.1 8B/70B); aggregate MuSR scores for thousands of open models: https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-llm-leaderboard/contents (their per-sample detail sets were not reachable without login)
musr.summary: 756 generated narratives (250 murder mysteries with 2 suspects, 256 object placements with 3-4 locations, 250 team allocations with 3 options) that need multi-step commonsense reasoning; humans score 94-100%. A good bbeh-like chat stand-in with per-question results for 14 models; note it was a Yugos public set in pack v0.3.0 (45 questions), not in the live v0.4.0 pack.

chat.why: One-line factual recall questions (real Google queries) with short reference answers, like simpleqa_verified, but on popular facts and graded by exact match against an incomplete answer list.

math_code.why: different skill: factual recall, no math or code

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, one text question with a short answer

1.model: Llama 3 8B (HELM Lite NaturalQuestions closed-book F1, 1,000 NQ dev questions, 5-shot)

nq_open.results_where: https://storage.googleapis.com/crfm-helm-public/lite/benchmark_output/releases/v1.13.0/groups/core_scenarios.json (NaturalQuestions closed-book, 91 models, per-instance predictions under runs/<suite>/natural_qa:mode=closedbook,...; HELM's NQ sample, not exactly the nq_open split)
nq_open.summary: 87,925 train + 3,610 validation short factual questions from Google search logs with lists of short answers (Wikipedia-answerable). Many easy simpleqa-style recall questions, useful as an easy chat stand-in, but the answer lists are incomplete, so even GPT-4o only reaches ~0.50 F1 (HELM) and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct 0.449 with a lenient contains-match (arXiv 2605.29648): re-grade with a judge before use.

chat.why: Elementary-science 4-option multiple choice (like ARC), short prompts and a letter answer; easier and narrower than mmlu_pro.

math_code.why: different skill: science multiple choice, almost no math

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, one text question with a short answer

openbookqa.summary: 5,957 grade-school science questions (4,957 train / 500 val / 500 test) with 4 options, built around a small 'open book' of science facts (the additional config gives the fact and a human score). Easy (2024 flagships ~97%), so a stand-in for the very easy private chat part, with per-question results for 91 models in HELM Lite.

chat.why: Binary paraphrase classification of two Wikipedia sentences with high word overlap: a short checkable label, but a classification skill rather than question answering or reasoning.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, sentence-pair classification

paws.licence: free to use for any purpose, with acknowledgement of Google (repo LICENSE); HF lists 'other'
paws.summary: PAWS-Wiki labeled pairs (49,401 train / 8,000 dev / 8,000 test, 44% paraphrases) made by word swapping and back-translation; PAWS-QQP cannot be redistributed. It is in the Yugos catalog (run via Inspect Evals), so it could appear in a private chat set, but no published scores for current model groups on the English test were found (only near-chance Llama 3 8B results on the multilingual PAWS-X), so no level anchors.

chat.why: Two-choice everyday physical commonsense (pick the better solution to a goal): short prompt and a checkable choice, but a commonsense topic not in the public chat mix.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, one text question with a short answer

2.model: GPT-4o / Claude 3.5 Sonnet (mean of 0.955 and 0.945, zero-shot direct)

piqa.questions_where: https://yonatanbisk.com/piqa/ (train/dev with labels; HF ybisk/piqa uses a loading script)
piqa.summary: Goal + two candidate solutions about physical everyday tasks (16,113 train, 1,838 labelled dev, 3,084 test with hidden labels). In the Yugos catalog and very easy for 2024 flagships (~95%), so a plausible stand-in for the easy private chat part, with 14 models' per-question results on the dev set.

chat.why: One-line factual recall about Wikidata entities, many long-tail (like simpleqa_verified), short answer checked against alias lists; questions are templated from 16 relation types.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, one text question with a short answer

popqa.summary: 14,267 templated questions (e.g. 'What is George Rankin's occupation?') from Wikidata triples, with subject popularity (page views) and answer aliases. A large simpleqa-style recall set whose popularity field gives an easy-to-hard knob; group-2 scores were only found on the 1,399-question long-tail subset (GPT-4-turbo-2024-04-09 0.335, GPT-3.5-turbo-1106 0.322 accuracy, RankRAG paper), so only one anchor is given.

chat.why: Read a PubMed abstract (~350 tokens) and answer a research question yes/no/maybe: short checkable answer like reading QA, but narrow biomedical topic and noisy labels (human 78%).

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, one text question with a short answer

2.model: GPT-4o (2024-05-13) / Claude 3.5 Sonnet (20241022) (MedHELM v4, 1,000 items, mean of 0.701 and 0.744)

pubmedqa.questions_where: qiaojin/PubMedQA (pqa_labeled; test = 500 PMIDs in github.com/pubmedqa/pubmedqa data/test_ground_truth.json)
pubmedqa.results_where: MedHELM v4.0.0 (13 models incl. GPT-5, GPT-4o, Claude 3.5/3.7 Sonnet, DeepSeek R1): https://storage.googleapis.com/crfm-helm-public/medhelm/benchmark_output/releases/v4.0.0/groups/pubmed_qa.json ; per-instance display_predictions.json under https://storage.googleapis.com/crfm-helm-public/medhelm/benchmark_output/runs/v4.0.0/
pubmedqa.summary: 1,000 expert-labelled yes/no/maybe questions (55% yes) over PubMed abstracts, plus 61k unlabelled and 211k auto-generated ones. In the Yugos catalog; scores are flat at ~0.72-0.75 from GPT-3.5 to GPT-5 because of label noise, so about a quarter of questions are effectively unsolvable noise for a router, but 13 models' per-question results are public (MedHELM).

chat.why: Grade-school science 8-option multiple choice that combines two facts, short prompt and a letter answer; easier and narrower than mmlu_pro.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, one text question with a short answer

qasc.summary: 9,980 8-option science questions (8,134 train / 926 val / 920 test with hidden answers) each built from two composed facts, with a 17M-sentence corpus. An easy MC stand-in for the private chat part; no published scores for current model groups were found, so no level anchors.

chat.why: 4-option multiple choice about a long article or story (~4,800 words, ~6,000 tokens), so reading QA with a letter answer but about 4x longer than Yugos chat prompts.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, long-document multiple choice

quality.summary: 6,737 questions on 381 long English passages (train 2,523 / dev 2,086 labelled; test 2,128 hidden), about half marked HARD; written by people who read the whole text. Tests long-context reading more than Yugos's short chat prompts; each article carries its own licence field.

chat.why: Read a ~400-token passage from a Chinese high-school English exam and pick one of 4 options: reading-comprehension QA with a letter answer, easier than hotpotqa.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, one text question with a short answer

race_h.licence: non-commercial research use only (CMU terms; passages not CMU property); HF lists 'other'
race_h.summary: RACE-high: 62,445 train / 3,451 val / 3,498 test 4-option questions (test: 1,045 passages, median ~1,700 characters). In the Yugos catalog and a likely-easy reading MC stand-in for the private chat part; only base-model cloze scores were found (Llama 3 8B 54.3 on combined RACE, not comparable), so no level anchors.

chat.why: Crowdsourced school science 4-option questions (physics, chemistry, biology), often with a support paragraph that contains the answer; easy knowledge MC.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, one text question with a short answer

sciq.summary: 13,679 science exam questions (11,679 / 1,000 / 1,000) with one answer, three distractors and usually a support passage. Easy science MC for the private chat part (non-commercial licence); no published scores for the four model groups were found, so no level anchors.

chat.why: Same questions, answer format and judge grading as the live simpleqa_verified set, which was filtered from it.

simpleqa.overlap: Contains the live simpleqa_verified set: SimpleQA Verified is filtered from SimpleQA (944 questions overlap per the rubric); drop those before use.
simpleqa.summary: 4,326 short fact-seeking questions written to make GPT-4o/GPT-3.5 hallucinate, each with one time-stable answer, graded correct/incorrect/not attempted by a model judge (Yugos pins gpt-5.4-mini). Questions outside SimpleQA Verified are the best direct extra data for the simpleqa_verified part.
